sections.label: TSIB as investigating authority
sections.summary: The Transport Safety Investigation Bureau, a Ministry of Transport department, will conduct safety investigations into air, sea and certain land transport incidents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB), a department of the Ministry of Transport, will be the authority responsible for conducting safety investigations into air, sea and certain land transport incidents.

sections.label: No-blame principles extended to rail
sections.summary: The TSIB Bill extends no-blame safety investigation principles, processes and best practices from air and marine sectors to the rail sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The TSIB Bill will extend the no-blame safety investigation principles, processes and best practices from the air and marine sectors to the rail sector.

sections.label: Powers of TSIB investigators
sections.summary: Clauses 26 to 31 confer powers on TSIB investigators, including accessing occurrence sites, gathering information and records, taking evidence and requiring medical examinations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: To ensure that investigators are able to effectively perform their roles, clauses 26 to 31 of the Bill confer on TSIB investigators the necessary powers, including powers to access occurrence sites, gather information and records, take possession of evidence, and require medical examinations of persons involved.

sections.label: High Court disclosure of restricted information
sections.summary: Clause 43 subsection 4 allows the High Court to order disclosure of restricted information if public interest in justice outweighs adverse impact on investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Subsection 4 of clause 43, however, allows the High Court to order the disclosure of any restricted information, if the High Court is satisfied that any adverse domestic or international impact that the disclosure might have on any current or future investigation is outweighed by the public interest in the administration of justice.

sections.label: Extending powers to rail and buses
sections.summary: The Bill proposes extending the TSIB's investigative powers to rail and LTA-contracted buses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, it would be beneficial for the TSIB's investigative powers to be extended to two other modes of transport, rail and LTA-contracted buses, as proposed in this Bill.

sections.label: Recovering investigator remuneration and expenses
sections.summary: The clause allows the Director of the TSIB to recover a reasonable part of an investigator's remuneration and expenses from transport vehicle owners or operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The clause states, "the Director of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau may recover from the owner or operator of a transport vehicle or both, a reasonable part of the remuneration of an investigator; and all expenses reasonably incurred by an investigator in the exercise of any powers." Can I clarify with the Minister under what circumstances would these costs be borne by TSIB, and under what circumstances would it be borne by transport owners or operators?

sections.label: Maximum duration of detainment
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there is a maximum duration for such detainment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can I clarify if there is a maximum duration for such detainment?

sections.label: Transport vehicle exemption classes
sections.summary: The passage asks if certain transport vehicle classes are contemplated for exemption and what circumstances govern exemptions, and states the Bill tasks TSIB with investigating transport incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if there are certain classes of transport vehicles that are currently in contemplation for exemption?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Are there specific circumstances which would govern an exemption that can be made known in this Bill?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill tasks TSIB with the mission of investigating incidents relating to aviation, marine, rail and public transport with a view to enhancing transport safety and preventing accidents or the recurrence of accidents.

sections.label: TSIB role and blame
sections.summary: The passage states clause 9 gives TSIB the role of independently investigating occurrences, identifying contributing factors and reporting publicly, and clause 9(3) says assigning blame and liability is not its function.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to clause 9 of the Bill, TSIB's role is to independently investigate occurrences, identify factors that have contributed to the occurrence and report publicly on those investigations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, clause 9(3) makes it clear that assigning blame and liability is not the function of TSIB.

sections.label: TSIB report admissible at Coroner's Inquiry
sections.summary: The passage states that under clause 21 the TSIB report will be admissible before a Coroner's Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Further, according to clause 21 of the Bill, the TSIB report will be admissible before a Coroner's Inquiry.

sections.label: TSIB staffing with professionals
sections.summary: The passage asks how TSIB will be staffed with sufficient professionals with necessary skills to collate information, analyse near-miss patterns and anticipate weak links for preventative measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Minister explain how will TSIB be staffed with sufficient professionals with the necessary skills to collate information, analyse and study the patterns of near-misses and anticipate weak links so that preventative measures can be drawn up and implemented?

sections.label: Staff training and transferred investigations
sections.summary: The passage asks whether staff earmarked for Statutory Board jobs will be sent abroad for training and how many ongoing investigations by other Government agencies will transfer to TSIB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Will staff who are earmarked for jobs in the Statutory Board be sent abroad for training?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Also, how many investigations are currently ongoing, being conducted by other Government agencies, which will be transferred to the TSIB umbrella?

sections.label: Penalty, TSIB, transport safety investigations
sections.summary: The passage states the penalty for non-compliance, calls for a higher minimum fine, and supports a Bill enabling TSIB to investigate transport incidents across air, land and sea.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The penalty for failure to comply without a reasonable excuse is a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or both.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The penalty should be more punitive and set at a minimum of $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This Bill is a representation of the Government’s determination to shore up safety lapses and provide a safer transport system worthy of a regional and international transport hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It also brings with it potential for greater interest and development in safety and risk management, which could lead to more careers in a meaningful industry that saves lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: My members include public rail workers and public bus workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I stand in support of the Bill which seeks to enable TSIB to conduct independent safety investigations into transport incidents, across the air, land and sea domains.

sections.label: Public bus accident investigation provisions
sections.summary: The speaker asks why the TSI Bill has specific provisions for investigations into public bus accidents, as they do not cover bus accidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As they do not cover bus accidents, I am curious as to why the TSI Bill has catered specific provisions for investigations into public bus accidents.

sections.label: Autonomous public transport investigation powers
sections.summary: The passage states autonomous buses and shuttles will be deployed in Punggol, Tengah and the Jurong Innovation District in 2022, and TSIB should be empowered to investigate incidents involving them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Autonomous buses and shuttles are soon to be deployed in Punggol, Tengah and the Jurong Innovation District in 2022, and TSIB should also be empowered to investigate any incidents involving such autonomous public transport, should an unfortunate accident happen in Singapore.

sections.label: TSIB investigation numbers
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry to shed light on how many investigations TSIB conducts yearly and the estimated number it would be expected to investigate annually in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Ministry could also shed light into how many investigations TSIB typically conducts in a year, and the estimated number of incidents TSIB would be expected to investigate annually in the future.

sections.label: TSIB creation from Air Accident Investigation Bureau
sections.summary: The passage states TSIB was administratively created in August 2016, coming out of the Air Accident Investigation Bureau.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: TSIB was administratively created in August 2016, coming out of the Air Accident Investigation Bureau.

sections.label: Building rail safety investigation capabilities
sections.summary: The passage states that is not currently planned, and rail safety investigation capabilities will be built up over the next two years through recruitment and training of rail safety investigators.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, that is not something that we are currently planning on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are planning to build up our rail safety investigation capabilities over the next two years through the recruitment and training of rail safety investigators.

sections.label: TSIB investigating LTA-contracted bus incidents
sections.summary: The provision allows TSIB to be activated to investigate incidents involving LTA-contracted bus services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As has been noted, we have included the provision for TSIB to be activated to investigate incidents involving LTA-contracted bus services.

sections.label: TSI Bill unmanned vehicle investigations
sections.summary: The TSI Bill provides for investigating incidents involving unmanned aircraft, vessels, rail vehicles, and, at the Minister's direction, LTA-contracted unmanned buses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The TSI Bill does provide for the investigation of incidents involving unmanned aircraft, unmanned vessels, unmanned rail vehicles, and, at the Minister's direction, unmanned buses which operate on services contracted by LTA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There were a number of questions about military vehicles and exemptions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This is a requirement under international agreements that transport safety investigations are not conducted into occurrences involving only military and state transport vehicles.

sections.label: TSIB aviation and marine investigations average
sections.summary: In the past two years, TSIB initiated an average of 17 investigations into aviation and marine incidents per year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In the past two years, TSIB has initiated an average of 17 investigations into aviation and marine incidents per year.

sections.label: Limits on detaining transport vehicles
sections.summary: Clause 30, paragraph 5 states the Director must not detain a transport vehicle longer than necessary and reasonable to exercise other powers under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Clause 30, paragraph 5, explicitly says "The Director must not detain a transport vehicle under this section for longer than is necessary and reasonable to exercise any other powers under this Act." The transport vehicle can only be detained for both what is necessary and reasonable to facilitate the investigations.

sections.label: High Court ordering restricted information disclosure
sections.summary: Under clause 43, paragraph 4, the High Court may order disclosure of restricted information if satisfied it is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Under clause 43, paragraph 4, the High Court may order the disclosure of the restricted information if it is satisfied that this is necessary.

sections.label: Information sharing within legal frameworks
sections.summary: If information is shared, it is done within the regulatory and legal frameworks for each investigation and agency.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: If there is sharing of information, it is done within the regulatory and legal frameworks for each investigation and for each agency.

sections.label: Draft report and TSIB independence
sections.summary: Making the draft report available is an international aviation practice that increases public confidence and completes fact-finding, while the Bill gives TSIB independence from commercial interests.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked particularly about the issue of making the draft report available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This is a practice that has been happening in the aviation industry, particularly, internationally, and the commercial players see value in this because it increases public confidence in the safety of the processes – their processes as well as the international agreements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It should be seen not as a vetting of the final report but as a completion of the fact-finding and analysis of the information that is there and how experts interpret what has happened.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But ultimately, the positioning of where TSIB sits within the Ministry, its protections under the law, and the structure of their operations as regulated by this Bill give it that independence from commercial interests.

sections.label: Penalty for failing administrative cooperation
sections.summary: The penalty is for failing to administratively cooperate with TSIB and respond to safety recommendations, not for a safety lapse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This is not the penalty for a safety lapse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This is a penalty for failing to administratively cooperate with TSIB and respond to safety recommendations.
